answer: Reward slots that decay with similarity make cloned output worthless. Each identity holds a few paid slots per epoch, and every result is compared against the append-only cedar archive of past outputs; the closest earlier entry becomes its anchor. Each further head matching that anchor drops one terrace on the payout schedule, and each terrace pays half the one above. A farm cannot reuse one solve: every head must fund distinct reasoning or earn geometrically less. Honest agents seldom share an anchor; single-answer tasks collide, so those go unscored.
